name: tiana-co-seller-compliance
description: Free US compliance checks for marketplace sellers: which safety certificate a product needs, what Amazon, Walmart, TikTok Shop and Etsy ask for, whether a supplier is on a US blacklist, what changed this week, and what a customs hold means.

interface.longDescription:
For marketplace sellers and small importers selling in the United States.

Ask in your own words which US safety certificate or import paperwork a product needs: a Children's Product Certificate (CPC) or a General Certificate of Conformity (GCC), FCC authorization for electronics, or FDA's import steps for food and supplements (facility registration, prior notice, FSVP), cosmetics, drugs and medical devices. Ask what Amazon, Walmart, TikTok Shop, Etsy, stores or your own website will ask for it, whether a supplier is on a US forced-labor or sanctions list (the UFLPA Entity List, CBP withhold release orders, the OFAC lists and the Consolidated Screening List), and what changed in seller rules this week. Ask what a hold means for a shipment held by US customs: from the seller's answers to up to three questions about the notice, the hold type, the response deadline or where to find it on the notice, and the documents usually needed, each cited. Every answer names its government or marketplace source, the date it was read, and a link to the free check on tiana-co.com. The supplier check reads the name as typed and is not a record.

It does not classify goods, give duty rates, give legal advice, or prepare or file anything for customs: a licensed customs broker files the entry. It covers the United States only. It never reads documents, never takes payment, and asks for no account. It never reads a customs notice itself, and it does not write, argue or file a response to CBP.
defaultPrompt: Does my kids' raincoat need a CPC?
Can I sell toys on Amazon?
CBP is holding my shipment. What does the notice mean, and how long do I have?

positive.description: A children's product: which certificate it needs, and the questions that decide the rules.
positive.prompt: Does my kids' raincoat need a CPC?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls which_certificate with the product (and made_for_children "yes" when the user's words say it is for kids). The result says the raincoat points to a Children's Product Certificate (CPC), that no FCC or FDA step applies, and lists the questions that decide which safety rules the certificate covers (for example sleepwear, vinyl film, and whether it is a hat or gloves), each with its answer values. The assistant asks the user those questions and can call again with the answers. The result names Tiana & Co. as the source and links to the free plan on tiana-co.com.

positive.description: A shipment held by US customs: what kind of hold, the deadline, and the usual documents.
positive.prompt: I got a CBP Form 4647 for my shipment of ceramic planters. What is it and how long do I have?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls shipment_held without answers, because the tool never sees the notice. It returns up to three questions about what the notice says (whether it mentions forced labor, another agency such as CPSC, FDA or FCC, or a stated reason such as a CF-28 or CF-29), with their answer keys. After the user answers, a second call returns the hold type, the response deadline or where to find it on the notice, the usual path and who leads it, and the documents usually needed, each cited to its CBP or federal source with the date it was read. It does not read the notice, predict a release, or write a response to CBP.

positive.description: Selling a product on a marketplace: what that marketplace and federal law will ask for.
positive.prompt: Can I sell toys on Amazon?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls marketplace_asks with the product "toys" and the channel amazon. Whether the toys are made mainly for children 12 or under decides the certificate, so the first result asks that one question. After the answer, a second call returns Amazon's own rules for toys and the US federal law that applies everywhere, each line numbered to its source with the page's date and the day it was read, and a link to the free plan. It does not promise that a listing will be approved.

positive.description: A supplier checked against US forced-labor and sanctions lists.
positive.prompt: Is Jiangmen Silverlake Plastics Co., Ltd. on the UFLPA entity list?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls screen_supplier with the company name. Returns, for each of five US lists (the UFLPA Entity List, CBP withhold release orders, the OFAC SDN List, the OFAC Consolidated List and the US Consolidated Screening List), match, possible match, no match or not searched, with the number of entries searched and the list's date. For this made-up name, no match on all five. It says it checked the name as typed, not a confirmed company, and that it is not a record, and links to the site to confirm which company it is.

positive.description: This week's changes to US seller rules.
positive.prompt: Any new seller rules this week for Amazon or Walmart?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls what_changed. Returns the latest weekly issue: each change with its marketplace or federal source, the page's own date and the day it was checked, and names the pages that could not be checked that week. The assistant answers for Amazon and Walmart from that list, and says so when neither changed.

negative.description: Customs classification and duty rates are out of scope (only a licensed customs broker classifies goods for an entry).
negative.prompt: What's the HTS code and duty rate for ceramic mugs from China?

negative.description: Filling out or filing a customs entry is out of scope (a licensed customs broker files the entry).
negative.prompt: Fill out my customs entry for a shipment of plush toys arriving next week.

negative.description: Rules outside the United States are out of scope.
negative.prompt: What does the EU require to sell toys in Germany? Do I need CE marking?

publication.release_notes: First release: five free, read-only checks for US marketplace sellers.
